newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia scraps state oil export programmes -Nemtsov.
newsitem.headline: Russia scraps state oil export programmes -Nemtsov.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has signed a decree scrapping government-sponsored exports of crude oil under so-called federal programmes, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Wednesday.

"The point of the decree is to halt the existence of the so-called state export programmes of giving quotas to export Russian oil," he told a closed news briefing, a tape of which was obtained by Reuters.
"The point of the decree is to scrap the programme and to give oil companies the possibility to export independently."

"You probably know that a lot of oil was supplied for state needs, and to our great regret, the effectiveness of the programmes was very low," Nemtsov said. He did not say when the programmes would be scrapped, but the move is not expected to affect Russia's overall oil export volumes.

Quarterly federal programme deliveries are about four million tonnes, or 15-16 percent of Russia's total annual crude exports. Russia exported 125.6 million tonnes (2.51 million barrels per day) of oil to all destinations in 1996.

Nemtsov said scrapping the programmes would help oil companies pay more overdue taxes directly into the budget and allow producers to pay off three trillion roubles ($521 million) in debts to the state by the end of the year.
Federal programmes are a Soviet-era leftover which Moscow has used to raise cash for projects ranging from satellite launches to factory construction.
